hints: Look at what each m/e value actually represents, remembering the sample is only boron plus aluminium impurity.
Identify X+ and Y+ as the two isotopes of boron and Z+ as aluminium, then compare their protons and electrons as 1+ ions.
For the Ar of boron, use only the two boron peaks and remember to rescale their abundances to 100% for boron alone.
walkthrough:
**Identify the three ions**

Boron has two isotopes with mass numbers 10 and 11, so X+ is $^{10}\text{B}^{+}$ and Y+ is $^{11}\text{B}^{+}$. Aluminium has mass number 27, so Z+ is $^{27}\text{Al}^{+}$.

**Check statement 1 about electrons**

A neutral B atom (Z = 5) has 5 electrons, so $\text{B}^{+}$ has 4 electrons. A neutral Al atom (Z = 13) has 13 electrons, so $\text{Al}^{+}$ has 12 electrons.

$$\text{electrons in Z}^{+} = 13 - 1 = 12 > 4 = 5 - 1 = \text{electrons in X}^{+}$$
So statement 1 is correct.

**Check statement 3 about protons**

X+ and Y+ are isotopes of the same element, boron. Isotopes have the same proton number but different neutron numbers.

$$\text{protons in X}^{+} = \text{protons in Y}^{+} = 5$$
So statement 3 is incorrect.

**Calculate Ar of boron correctly**

Ar of boron must use only boron isotopes, so ignore the 10.00% aluminium and rescale to the boron total.

$$\text{total B abundance} = 15.52 + 74.48 = 90.00$$
$$A_r(\text{B}) = \frac{(10 \times 15.52) + (11 \times 74.48)}{90.00} = \frac{974.48}{90.00} = 10.83$$
To four significant figures this is 10.83, so statement 2 is correct.

**Conclude the combination**

Statements 1 and 2 only are correct. This matches option B.

options.A: Incorrect because it requires all three statements. Statement 3 is wrong since X+ and Y+ are both boron ions with 5 protons each, they differ in neutrons, not protons.
options.B: Correct because statements 1 and 2 only are true. Z+ ($\text{Al}^{+}$) has 12 electrons versus 4 in X+ ($^{10}\text{B}^{+}$), and the renormalised boron Ar is 10.83.
options.C: Incorrect because it requires 2 and 3. Statement 3 is false for isotopes, and it wrongly leaves out the true statement 1 about electrons.
options.D: Incorrect because it claims only statement 1. Statement 2 is also true when you correctly calculate Ar using only the boron abundances (total 90.00, not 100).
